name: figure-with-data-table
description: A chart. APG has no pattern for one, so this is Arena's own, adopted from WCAG 1.1.1 rather than invented: a picture nobody can read is not an alternative, so every chart pairs a labelled graphic with a real table of its numbers. The table is visually hidden, not absent. A role="img" subtree is presentational, so nothing focusable inside the graphic reaches a screen reader however correct its ARIA; that one fact splits the pattern in two. A screen reader gets the table, which is already here. A sighted keyboard user gets a data cursor that moves exactly what hover moves: the emphasised mark, the crosshair and the tooltip, whose numbers were reachable by pointer alone (WCAG 2.1.1). The cursor walks the CATEGORY axis, so which arrow pair moves it is a property of the chart and not of the pattern: a chart states the pair it does not use as an exception rather than answering four keys, because a chart that consumed ArrowUp would take the page scroll away from a reader who only wanted to leave it. A plot with two category axes, a heatmap's rows and columns, is the one case that answers both pairs, so while it has focus the four arrows are its own and Tab leaves it. The cursor's tooltip is not announced, because the data table is the screen reader's channel and browse mode takes the arrow keys first. A hidden listbox of options mirroring the marks was weighed and refused: it is a second copy of the same numbers in the same DOM, and one source per fact is the rule that copy would break. This describes what both chart layers already do, not an aspiration.

requires.roles.label: aria-label naming the chart
requires.alternative.table: a real <table> of the plotted numbers, visually hidden
requires.focus.roving: one tab stop for the whole plot; the data cursor moves within it and never adds a second stop
requires.keyboard.ArrowLeft: moves the data cursor to the previous point, clamping at the first
requires.keyboard.ArrowRight: moves the data cursor to the next point, clamping at the last
requires.keyboard.ArrowUp: moves the data cursor to the previous point, clamping at the first, on a chart whose categories run down the plot rather than across it
requires.keyboard.ArrowDown: moves the data cursor to the next point, clamping at the last, on a chart whose categories run down the plot rather than across it
requires.keyboard.Home: moves the data cursor to the first point
requires.keyboard.End: moves the data cursor to the last point
